scope: Truthfulness (data-backing) only. Not a quality, SEO, or hallucination-detection audit. Classification rules: supported = comes directly from structured data; computed = derived deterministically with no missing state; disclosed-missing = the page honestly states or silently omits an unknown; fallback = the generator substitutes generic prose that reads as a specific claim.

name-detail-page.assertion: Groups/links the name by its first letter
name-detail-page.backingDataset: data/names.json (first_letter) — deterministic first character of the name string
name-detail-page.note: Classified as computed, not supported, because it is a deterministic transform of the name string with no possible missing state (per Phase 1C classification rules, matching the brief's own "Letter" example).

name-detail-page.assertion: Lists spelling variants of the name
name-detail-page.note: Classified as computed (per the brief's explicit "Variants" example) since variant generation is a deterministic phonetic/spelling transform, not per-name research.

name-detail-page.assertion: FAQ answers "Is {name} a biblical name?" with Yes or No
name-detail-page.note: Always renders, but always accurately reflects data/categories.json either way (Yes for the 1 biblical-tagged name, No for the other 3696) — a binary claim that is truthful in both branches, unlike the meaning/origin fallbacks. Classified supported, not fallback, because the "No" answer is not a generic substitute; it is the correct answer given the data.

name-detail-page.assertion: States what the name "means" in the meta description / direct-answer / FAQ lead
Shows the name's meaning in the Quick Facts table
name-detail-page.note:
The "—

" marker is coarse: it also fires for other unrelated empty fields on the same page (e.g. a missing rank), so the exact page count for meaning specifically is an upper bound, not a precise isolation. The qualitative classification (honest placeholder, not fabrication) is verified regardless.

name-detail-page.assertion: Describes the name's "Origin and Linguistic Lineage"
Describes the name's "Historical and Cultural Context"
FAQ answers "Where does the name {name} come from?"
Describes the name's "Name Usage & Cultural Context"
FAQ answers "How popular is the name {name}?"

name-detail-page.note: phonetic coverage is exactly 0%, so this section is omitted on all 3,697 pages — the maximal case of an honest, silent non-claim.

names-like-page.backingDataset: data/names.json (name string only — first letter / prefix match)
names-like-page.note: Requires only the name string itself, so it is populated for effectively every name; classified computed (deterministic string match), not supported (no per-name research involved).

names-like-page.assertion: Lists names with "the Same Origin" (section omitted when none found)

evidence.method: phase1b-coverage (proxy: section renders only when origin data exists, so its absence rate tracks origin_country_or_language coverage)

names-like-page.assertion: Lists names with "Similar Popularity" (section omitted when none found)

evidence.method: phase1b-coverage (gender is the guaranteed fallback dimension)

sibling-harmony-page.assertion: States a Harmony score / percentage between two names
sibling-harmony-page.backingDataset: computed (generate-sibling-harmony.js: origin 30% + rhythm 25% + popularity 20% + length 15% + style 10%)

sibling-harmony-page.assertion: States the base name's origin as part of the "Shared origin" scoring factor
sibling-harmony-page.backingDataset: data/names.json (origin_country/language — NOTE: unenriched dataset, see note)
sibling-harmony-page.note: generate-sibling-pages.js loads data/names.json, not data/names-enriched.json, so this fires at 100% even for names whose own name-detail page has real origin data.

sibling-harmony-page.assertion: States syllable count / first letter as part of the "Phonetic rhythm" scoring factor
States a popularity band ("top 100" / "other") as part of the "Popularity parity" scoring factor
sibling-harmony-page.generatorFunction: sibling-explanation-renderer.js :: buildContext() (defaults popBand to "other" when no rows exist)

evidence.method: source-verified only — the 150-name sibling batch cannot be reconstructed from the 5-name-deep popularity dataset (see audit/knowledge-density.json limitation), so an exact page count cannot be measured; this record's evidence is Unknown by count, not by mechanism.

sibling-harmony-page.note: "other" is a generic bucket label, not a specific fabricated claim (contrast with the meaning/origin fallbacks) — classified disclosed-missing.

surname-compatibility-page.assertion: States a first-name/surname compatibility score or ranking
surname-compatibility-page.backingDataset: computed (scoreCompatibility(): syllable balance, vowel/consonant endings, phonetic flow, length harmony)

surname-compatibility-page.assertion: Shows a "Heraldry and Family Heritage" section (omitted when unavailable)

minorityPath.when: heraldry.json has available:true for this surname

names-lastname-filter-page.assertion: States a first-name/surname compatibility score or ranking
names-lastname-filter-page.backingDataset: computed (scoreCompatibility(): syllable balance, vowel/consonant endings, phonetic flow, length harmony)

equivalents-page.assertion: Lists cross-linguistic equivalents of the anchor name
equivalents-page.note: The page only exists for the 27 anchors present in the dataset, so by construction every instance is backed by real curated data.

compare-name-country-pair-page.assertion: States each country's current popularity rank for the name
compare-name-country-pair-page.backingDataset: data/popularity.json (via getRank(), computed independently of data/country-differentials.json)

evidence.method: source-verified (all 4 compared names have at least one real popularity row)

compare-name-country-pair-page.note: audit/knowledge-dependencies.json (Phase 1B) attributed this page to data/country-differentials.json; Phase 1C source verification found generate-compare-pages.js never reads that file — it computes rank/movement/volatility directly from data/popularity.json instead. This is a correction to the Phase 1B chain, noted here rather than silently changed there.

compare-name-country-pair-page.assertion: States the 10-year rank movement / trend delta between two countries
compare-name-country-pair-page.backingDataset: data/popularity.json (requires a year-2015 row, which does not exist for any name)

compare-name-country-pair-page.assertion: Describes cultural/naming differences between the two countries
compare-name-country-pair-page.backingDataset: hardcoded per-pair static text blocks (getCulturalContext()), not derived from any per-name dataset
compare-name-country-pair-page.note: Same 5 static paragraphs (one per country pair) are reused verbatim for every name compared within that pair — deterministic and always reproducible, so classified computed rather than supported (it is not about the specific name at all).

names-country-page.assertion: Lists names associated with this country (explicit empty-state guard exists in source)
names-country-page.note: All 5 site-supported country pages have at least some matching names in practice; the empty-state guard exists but was not observed to trigger for any of the 5.

names-style-page.assertion: Lists names tagged with this style (explicit "No names in this style yet" fallback text exists in source)
names-style-page.generatorFunction: generateStylePage() ("No names in this style yet." literal)
names-style-page.note: An honest disclosed-missing message exists in source for empty style categories; whether any of the 7 live style pages actually trigger it was not individually re-verified in this pass (all 7 are treated as supported pending that check — see docs/TRUTHFULNESS_AUDIT.md limitations).

popularity-year-page.assertion: Lists top-ranked names for the year
popularity-year-page.note: Real data, just extremely sparse (7 rows shared across all 3 year pages) — not fabricated, so classified supported, not fallback.

trend-page.backingDataset: data/regional-trend-acceleration.json (2 of 5 site countries: USA, CAN)
trend-page.note: Covers only 2 of 5 countries, but the page does not claim broader coverage than that per its own title ("US 2025 vs 2015") — classified supported, not fallback.

notes: Every count in the evidence field is either grep-verified against real generated HTML (method: "grep-verified" / "live-data-count") or pulled from a prior Phase 1A/1B audit report (method: "phase1b-coverage") — no percentage in this file was estimated by inspection alone.

Where an assertion behaves differently depending on whether its backing data is present, ONE dominant state is recorded here (matching the majority real-world case) and the minority behavior is recorded in minorityPath — this keeps every assertion in exactly one of the four buckets as required, while still disclosing the alternate path.
